title: Rare-earth spin textures and a route to electronic inhomogeneity in $Pr_2Ir_2O_7$
authors: Kyle G Sherman, Michael J Lawler
abstract: The pyrochlore iridate $Pr_2Ir_2O_7$ remains metallic at low temperatures where its family members insulate. Recently, scanning tunneling spectroscopy experiments have revealed an inhomogeneous mixture of Kondo-screened and Kondo-destroyed regions when its surface is produced by cleaving at room temperature while it remains uniform when cleaved at low temperatures. We ask whether the frustrated praseodymium spin texture seeds this inhomogeneity. To study this, we produce Monte-Carlo-sampled Pr spin-ice configurations, presumed to evolve slowly in time, and couple through a local Kondo exchange $J_K$ to an eight-band Hartree-Fock model of the Ir electrons.   We further find the charge gap of the all-in-all-out state common in the other family members closes smoothly with the coupling $J_K$, and the recently proposed monopole-rich ``jellyfish'' textures further suppress the insulating behavior by $ΔJ_{Kc}\approx 0.03\,t$. Additionally, scanning a small cluster across a large Pr surface yields a synthetic tunneling map that fractures into islands within a sea. Although our classical simulable theory omits the Kondo singlet, the spatial modulation of the Fermi-level density of states it produces is, through the exponential Doniach sensitivity of the Kondo temperature, sufficient to tip the local balance between screening and magnetic order; a frustration-driven route to the observed Kondo/Kondo-destroyed inhomogeneity.
summary: This theoretical study investigates how the frustrated spin texture of Pr ions in $	ext{Pr}_2	ext{Ir}_2	ext{O}_7$ dictates its electronic properties. By coupling a spin-ice model to an Ir electronic Hamiltonian, the authors show that local variations in the Pr spins can induce a spatial pattern of electronic inhomogeneity. This suggests that frustration-driven local magnetism is the key mechanism driving the observed mixture of Kondo-screened and Kondo-destroyed electronic states.
main_problem: The study investigates whether the frustrated spin texture of the rare-earth element Pr in $	ext{Pr}_2	ext{Ir}_2	ext{O}_7$ is responsible for the observed electronic inhomogeneity, which manifests as a mixture of Kondo-screened and Kondo-destroyed regions.
main_result: The model successfully reproduces the inhomogeneous tunneling map, suggesting that local fluctuations in the Pr spin texture can drive the system into a frustration-driven regime exhibiting the observed Kondo/Kondo-destroyed electronic state.
method: The authors employed Monte Carlo sampling of classical Pr spin-ice configurations, coupling these to an eight-band Hartree-Fock model for the Ir electrons to calculate local density of states.
model_or_system: The system is the pyrochlore iridate $	ext{Pr}_2	ext{Ir}_2	ext{O}_7$. The electronic structure is modeled using an eight-band Hartree-Fock approach for Ir, coupled via a Kondo exchange interaction ($J_K$) to classical Pr spins treated via an effective spin-ice Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Local density of states ($ho(\mathbf{r}, 	ext{eV})$), gap closing, AIAO magnetic order parameter, and the ratio governing the local balance between Kondo screening and magnetic order ($T_K$ vs $T_{	ext{RKKY}}$).
important_parameters: Kondo coupling strength ($J_K$), the difference between 'ice' and 'jellyfish' textures ($\Delta J_{Kc} \approx 0.03 t$), and the local Fermi level density of states ($ho(	ext{EF})$).
main_assumptions: The Pr spins are treated as classical, static moments, and the simulation assumes the local electronic state is governed by the Doniach balance.
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates the dependence of the gap and AIAO order on $J_K$ for different Pr spin textures. Figure 3 presents a synthetic tunneling map showing insulating islands within a metallic sea across a simulated Pr surface.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by noting the experimental inhomogeneity in $	ext{Pr}_2	ext{Ir}_2	ext{O}_7$. It then develops a theoretical model coupling Pr spins to Ir electrons, simulating various Pr spin configurations. The results demonstrate how local Pr magnetism drives the system across phase boundaries, leading to the predicted inhomogeneous electronic structure.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical mechanism linking geometric frustration (Pr spin texture) to emergent electronic phenomena (Kondo screening breakdown) in strongly correlated oxides, which is highly relevant to understanding correlated materials physics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. The U-JK phase diagram of the coupled Pr-Ir model. Figures: praseodymium texture (left: spin ice, J = 0; right: jellyfish, J = 1/4). Columns: band gap (left) and AIAO order parameter (right), computed from the iridium Hartree-Fock mean field over Monte Carlo-sampled Pr configurations at T = 1 K on an N = 864 cluster. The AIAO insulator occupies large U; increasing JK smoothly closes the gap.
FIG. 2. Gap (a) and AIAO order (b) versus JK for Pr textures along the ice–jellyfish line. The critical coupling shifts by ∆JKc ≈0.03 t between endpoints.

FIG. 3. Synthetic local density of states over a 10 nm praseodymium field at T = 1 K, J = 1/4, U = 2.8, JK = 0.11. Insulating islands appear within a metallic sea. The praseodymium system contains 24,576 spins and the irid- ium system contains 864 sites.
